bundle.author: emilybgoodpartyorg
bundle.title: feat(elections): office names read the way voters say them
bundle.body:
Position pages and office rows were headed by election-api's normalised names: "City Legislature in Garden Grove, CA", "County Legislature-Executive Board in Orange County, CA", "Local Higher Education Board-Community College Board in San Diego County, CA" (Emily, 2026-10-08, QA pass).

A new helper, `officeDisplayName`, names an office the way voters say it:

1. For a local office (city, county, township, local, regional), BallotReady's own names for the seats behind the slug (`positionNames`, now requested on place races) are read, the seat part ("- District 3", "- At Large, Seat B", "(Term Commencing 1/2)") is dropped, and the page place's own name is taken off the front since the page already says where it is. "Garden Grove City Council" becomes "City Council", "Orange County Board of Supervisors" becomes "Board of Supervisors", "Harris County Commission" becomes "County Commission", "Livingston City Mayor" becomes "Mayor", "King County Executive" becomes "County Executive". A name that does not carry the place ("Louisville Metro Council") is kept whole. One odd BallotReady name is mapped by hand ("Indianapolis/Marion City/County Council" becomes "City-County Council").
2. When several BallotReady names sit behind one page (a county page lumping community college districts) or none are present, the normalised name goes through Emily's table (`OFFICE_NAME_FALLBACKS`: "City Legislature" to "City Council", "Local School Board" to "School Board", and so on), then a generic cleanup that drops "(Joint)" and keeps the first of hyphen-joined alternatives.
3. State and federal offices keep their normalised names on purpose: "State Representative" stays, as Emily asked.

Applied to the position page heading, title, breadcrumb and `[office name]` token on every position route, to the offices list rows on state, county, district and city pages, and to the nearby offices block. Carousel cards already use BallotReady's names. URLs and slugs are untouched. Tests cover the rule with the examples from Emily's county table (39 counties sampled from the live API), the mayor rule, the fallback table, the generic cleanup and the state exception.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Display-only naming for office list rows with fallbacks and tests; no routing, auth, or data writes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces election-api **normalised** office labels (e.g. "City Legislature") with voter-facing names on **location index office rows** and overlapping county/state lists.
> 
> Adds **`officeDisplayName`** (`src/lib/officeDisplayName.ts`): for local races it prefers BallotReady **`positionNames`** (now requested via `PLACE_RACE_COLUMNS`), strips seat suffixes and the page place name, then falls back to `OFFICE_NAME_FALLBACKS` and generic cleanup; **state/federal** offices keep normalised names. State, county, city, and district routes pass **`placeName`** into `buildOfficeItemsFromPlaceRaces` / `buildOverlappingOfficeItems` so stripping works. **URLs and slugs are unchanged.** Docs and unit tests cover Emily’s QA examples.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 03e7f4991b3e34b208d7cfa97c9962c3f6d2afaa. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

findings.body: All 8 position and candidates page `generateMetadata` functions still use `race?.normalizedPositionName ?? race?.name ?? 'Position'` (the raw API value) for `<title>` and meta description, while the page body now uses `officeDisplayName(race, race.Place)`. These diverge for every office the new helper rewrites: for example, a race with `normalizedPositionName = 'City Legislature'` gets a heading of "City Council" but a `<title>` of "City Legislature in …". The same mismatch applies to local offices whose BallotReady name is stripped of the place prefix ("Board of Supervisors" in the heading vs "Orange County Board of Supervisors" in meta). The inconsistency is visible in browser tabs, search-engine results, and social previews across all 8 position/candidates pages (state, county, city, and subplace variants). Falsification check: `officeDisplayName` would need to be a no-op to produce identical output — it is not; it applies `OFFICE_NAME_FALLBACKS`, `cleanNormalizedName`, place-name stripping, and the mayor rule.

output.summary: This PR introduces `officeDisplayName`, a display-name helper that rewrites election-api's normalised office labels (e.g. "City Legislature" → "City Council") for local races using BallotReady's own position names, a hand-curated fallback table, and generic cleanup. It is applied to office list rows on location pages (`buildOfficeItemsFromPlaceRaces`), to position page headings/breadcrumbs, and to nearby-offices blocks; state/federal offices intentionally keep their normalised names. The scout flagged four areas: (1) whether `positionNames` is fetched for position-detail pages — falsified, since `/v1/races` returns the full `RaceDetail` object including `positionNames` without needing `raceColumns`; (2) metadata inconsistency in `generateMetadata` — confirmed across all 8 position/candidates pages, where the page title and meta description still use the raw `normalizedPositionName` while the visible heading uses the new helper; (3) `stripSeat` splitting on ` - ` — falsified, as BallotReady's local-level naming consistently uses ` - ` only for seat/district designators; (4) missing `positionLevel` fallback — falsified, as `PLACE_RACE_COLUMNS` requests it and the fallback path is intentional graceful degradation. The human reviewer should confirm that the `generateMetadata` functions in the 8 position page files are updated to use `officeDisplayName` for consistency between meta tags and visible headings.
